subject: general
question: Which of the following types of coal is known to have the highest carbon content in it?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Anthracite__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most metamorphosed variety of coal is **anthracite**, also referred to as **hard coal**.
 
• Its calorific values, which are close to **35 megajoules per kilogramme** (15,000 British thermal units per pound), are equivalent to those of the bulk of bituminous coal.
 
• It possesses the most fixed carbon (86 percent or more) and the least volatile matter (14 percent or less on a dry, ash-free basis) of all the different forms of coal.
 
• The **most uncommon type** of coal is anthracite coal.
 
• Less than **2% of the US's total coal** reserves are found in it, largely in northeastern Pennsylvania.
 
• South Africa, Australia, the eastern Ukraine, western Canada, China, and other areas have less anthracite.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bituminous:**

 
 
• Up to **17 percent moisture** can be found in bituminous coal.
 
• Nitrogen makes up between **0.5 and 2 percent **of bituminous coal's weight.
 
• Up to **85% of its weight **can be made up of fixed carbon, while up to 12% of it can be made up of ash.
 
 
 
• **Lignite:**
 
 
• Lignite, often known as **brown coal** is a soft, brown, flammable sedimentary rock that was created when peat was naturally compacted.
 
• Due to its relatively low heat content, it is regarded as the lowest rank of coal and has a carbon concentration of between **25 and 35 percent**. 
 
• It has a **very high moisture content** when taken out of the ground, which contributes to its low carbon content. 
 
 
 
• **Sub-bituminous:**
 
 
• A **lower grade of coal **with a carbon content of **35–45%** is called sub-bituminous coal.
 
• This form of coal has qualities that fall between between bituminous coal, the second-highest grade of coal, and lignite, the lowest grade.
 
• Sub-bituminous coal is primarily **utilized as a fuel** for the production of steam-electric power.
